$comment: The 50 concepts the shipped library is built from. Each `text` is sent to the generator VERBATIM, exactly as typed here - the point is to test the generator and its prompt, not to hand-feed it GLSL. Ids are fixed so results files diff across rounds. Families exist so that coverage can be checked when a concept is swapped out; the brief allows up to 5 swaps, each with a recorded reason in docs/SHADER-LIBRARY.md.

flags.monochromeByDesign: Waives the chroma gate. The brief for this one really is a single hue or warm white, so low saturation is the ask rather than a washed-out failure.
flags.namesOwnColours: Waives the paletteFidelity gate. The description names specific colours, so rendering them instead of the user's arbitrary regression palette is obedience, not disobedience.
flags.bestAt: Set only after measurement, and only when a concept genuinely cannot be excellent at every shape. An honest bestAt is worth more than a shader that is mediocre everywhere. Null until a round proves otherwise.

families.light-show-canon: What people actually ask a light-show tool for. These must be excellent; a library that fumbles candy-cane has failed at its own job.
families.motion-background: The reference aesthetic: mesh gradients, chrome, iridescence, caustics, organic noise. Restraint in structure, boldness in colour.
families.natural: Phenomena. The test is whether it reads as the thing rather than as an abstract field with the word attached.
families.geometric: Built for props first. Bold, legible shapes that survive being 60 pixels wide and one pixel tall.
families.seasonal: Occasion pieces. Most name their own colours, which is the point of them.
